carryover.text: The /init-worktree skill's cone-mode sparse-checkout setup (git sparse-checkout init --cone; git sparse-checkout set <dirs>) can leave the underlying .git/worktrees/<name>/info/sparse-checkout file with non-cone patterns (/*, !*/) mixed in with the cone /<dir>/ entries. Git detects the invalid cone patterns, silently disables cone mode, and falls back to literal gitignore-style matching -- which does NOT recurse into subdirectories of the listed top-level dirs (e.g. planning/<spec-slug>/ vanishes even though planning/ itself is listed), so any file under a nested subdirectory (a new spec's tasks.md, in this case) is invisible in the worktree even though it's committed and tracked. Symptom: sdlc-flow errors with 'Missing spec' or 'No task headings' immediately after worktree creation, or a spec directory that git-ls-tree confirms exists on the branch is simply absent from `ls` in the worktree. Fix applied ad hoc this session: `git sparse-checkout init --cone` + `git sparse-checkout set $(git ls-tree HEAD --name-only -d | tr '\n' ' ')` again inside the broken worktree re-derives clean cone patterns and repopulates it -- no data loss, this is a checkout-view bug not a data bug. Root cause in the skill itself (why the first sparse-checkout set call produces non-cone patterns) was not investigated -- worth a fix in .claude/commands/init-worktree.md so future worktrees don't hit this, or at minimum add a post-creation verification step (git sparse-checkout list should show only clean /<dir>/ entries, no /* or !*/ lines).
carryover.clears_when: init-worktree.md is patched to prevent or auto-detect this failure mode, or the pattern is confirmed not to recur across several subsequent /init-worktree runs
